newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends weaker after US sparks profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends weaker after US sparks profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended heavily down on Friday having fallen victim to a burst of profit-taking after this week's NYMEX products rally ran out of steam.
March Brent closed 66 cents lower at $22.52 a barrel, just two cents off the session low. Despite the weak close, the contract still managed to hold onto gains of some 50 cents over the week.

Brent tracked NYMEX products futures which fell as dealers decided to liquidate long positions after this week's rally which had in part been stimulated by today's expiry of Feb NYMEX refined products contracts.
"People (in New York) settled their positions on Feb for the expiry and then started taking profits on March. We were just following that," said one IPE broker.
NYMEX March heating oil finished over two cents a gallon down at the session low of 66 cents a gallon.

IPE Feb gas oil earlier closed $2.75 lower at $209 a tonne, having rebounded off the session low of $206.50, just above a gap at $205.50. The March gas oil/Brent spread ended the week at $4 a barrel exactly.
Jeff Potter, managing director at Dublin-based Univest Ireland, said volume has been lighter the past few sessions which has increased the volatility.
"Overall it's still looking pretty negative," he said, adding the rally earlier this week was primarily a correction to the losses the previous two weeks.
But floor dealers said that March Brent still ended the week well above solid support at $22.00 a barrel.
"We did come off heavily but that's because heat was artificially high, not because of real fundamental weakness here," one said.
Forecasts for moderating weather in the U.S. Northeast, the world's largest heating oil market, next week helped to undermine the market, brokers said.
